question.text: What is the maximum loss for an option buyer and an option seller?

answer.text: Option buyer: maximum loss is the premium paid (limited). Option seller: maximum loss is theoretically unlimited for naked calls, or strike minus premium for naked puts
Both buyer and seller face unlimited losses
Both buyer and seller have losses limited to the premium amount
The option buyer can lose more than the premium due to margin calls

explanation.text: The Logic: Option buyers' losses are limited to the premium already paid, while option sellers' risk is unlimited. A naked call seller faces unlimited loss as the price can rise without bound; a naked put seller's loss at zero is K - Premium per unit. The Trap: Only sellers face potentially unlimited losses. Buyers never get margin calls because they have already paid the full premium upfront. Note: This asymmetry is why sellers must deposit margin while buyers do not.
